note: Forest Service campground in tall pines and young oaks on Laurel Lake, part of the Three Lakes-Eagle River Chain; a boat launch across from the parking area gives access to the whole chain. No swimming beach. Area 1 (sites 1-8) sits on a wooded knoll ringed by sedge marsh; Area 2 (9-12) lies about 300 m south beside a marsh channel. --Claude
summary: FS page + rec.gov facility/rates/catalog read. 12 nonelectric back-in sites (25-40 ft), $15, vault toilets, water; 7 reservable (3-5, 9-12) in peak season, 5 first-come; season 04-30..10-13 (manual, matches). WATERFRONT LEAD lakefront -> lakeview: both areas are set back from open water by sedge marsh and a tree band (Area 2 ~90 m to the lake); photos show filtered/marsh views. Closed for the season now (normal).
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (downgrade): stored lakefront -> lakeview. On Esri imagery Area 1 (sites 1-8, around 45.8155,-89.1098) is a wooded knoll surrounded by open sedge marsh; the open water of Laurel Lake lies ~100 m+ to the south-east across the marsh. Area 2 (sites 9-12, 45.81246-45.81316,-89.1109 to -89.1112) sits in pines beside the marsh: a ~10-20 m wide marsh channel lies ~20-25 m east of site 10, but the open lake is ~90 m east across sedge marsh and a band of trees. recreation.gov photos: site 12 looks across open grass to the marsh and channel, site 9 and site 6 show water only through trees. The stored evidence ('Area Two sites 9-12 open water w/ space to beach canoes') is not borne out: no site has open ground to the lake within ~50 m. rec.gov tags 2, 4-7 and 9-12 'Lakefront' (contrary claim). Proposed evidence: 'Esri imagery + rec.gov catalog/photos: Area 1 (1-8) on a wooded knoll ringed by sedge marsh, lake ~100 m+; Area 2 (9-12) ~90 m from open water across marsh and a tree band, marsh channel ~20 m from site 10; photos show filtered/marsh views - lakeview --Claude'.
